answer: Break the sybil multiplier with quadratic-cost influence. Agents spend voice credits to claim rewards, and each extra vote costs more than the last — so an operator splitting capital across a hundred puppets buys no more total sway than one honest agent spending the same sum. A dune of fake identities collapses under its own cost curve: a timber palisade of a hundred puppets pays a hundred times the expense for one seat of power, while honest agents pay once and play full-strength. To gain more, the farmer must concentrate — and a violet audit flag waits for the concentrated.
